title: GeneralizedLipschitzMinty.lean

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Unconstrained operator root finding. The continuous map F from ℝᵈ to ℝᵈ has a root z satisfying the Minty condition ⟨F(x), x−z⟩ ≥ 0 for every x.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: One query at any x returns the full vector F(x) exactly for every query history and oracle seed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x and y, ‖F(x)−F(y)‖ ≤ (L₀+L₁ max_{u∈[x,y]} ‖F(u)‖)‖x−y‖. Continuity ensures the segment maximum exists. The constants L₀ > 0 and L₁ ≥ 0 are public.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Queries, replies and outputs lie in the full Euclidean space ℝᵈ with public dimension d.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GeneralizedLipschitzMinty.lean, Params.d, spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.Output and spec.publicInput

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The public starting point x₀ and radius R ≥ 0 satisfy ‖x₀−z‖ ≤ R for the same hidden root z that satisfies the Minty condition.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The residual must be integrable and satisfy 𝔼[‖F(X)‖] ≤ ε under the product law of the algorithm and oracle seeds.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: The output is one point X in ℝᵈ. Its residual is the Euclidean operator norm ‖F(X)‖ to the first power, with public tolerance ε > 0.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines a Minty inequality about one hidden root with a Lipschitz bound that varies with the operator norm along each segment.

descriptionHtml:
Generalized Lipschitz Minty Root Finding

We seek a zero of a continuous operator F:Rd→Rd in Euclidean dimension d≥0. On each segment, F is Lipschitz with constant L0+L1M, where L0>0, L1≥0, and M is the maximum of ∥F∥ on that segment. A given starting point x0 lies within distance R≥0 of a zero x⋆ satisfying ⟨F(x),x−x⋆⟩≥0 for every x∈Rd. The oracle returns F(x) at x. For ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈Rd with E∥F(x¯)∥≤ε, where the expectation is over the algorithm’s randomness.

In terms of the Euclidean residual norm, the problem is minx∈Rd∥F(x)∥. The algorithm receives d∈{0,1,2,…}, L0, L1, R, ε, and x0∈Rd, and may query any point in Rd.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Generalized Lipschitz continuity). The operator F is continuous. For every x,y∈Rd, let Mx,y denote the maximum operator value in norm along the segment from x to y. Then Mx,y=maxt∈[0,1]∥F(x+t(y−x))∥,∥F(x)−F(y)∥≤(L0+L1Mx,y)∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Minty zero and initial distance). There exists x⋆∈Rd such that F(x⋆)=0, ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, and ⟨F(x),x−x⋆⟩≥0for every x∈Rd.

After the allotted oracle calls, the residual norm ∥F(x¯)∥ must be integrable under the law P of the algorithm’s randomness and satisfy EP[∥F(x¯)∥]≤ε.

theorems.referencesHtml: • Sayantan Choudhury and Nicolas Loizou. Extragradient Method for (L0,L1)-Lipschitz Root-finding Problems. NeurIPS 2025. Complexity: O(1+R2(L0/ε+L1)2) exact operator calls for adaptive extragradient to return a queried iterate with ∥F(x)∥≤ε.
theorems.formulaHtml: 2⋅(1+⌈32⋅(R⋅(L0ε+L1))2⌉+)

comparisonHtml:
A continuous F:Rd→Rd satisfies ∥F(x)−F(y)∥≤(L0+L1maxu∈[x,y]∥F(u)∥)∥x−y∥ for all x,y, with L0>0 and L1≥0. A root z satisfies ∥x0−z∥≤R and ⟨F(x),x−z⟩≥0 for all x. Calls return exact F(x). The target is ∫∥F(x^(ω))∥dP(ω)≤ε, with an integrable residual and ε>0. The displayed budgets suffice for deterministic residual at most ε.

Exact operator-call bounds for generalized Lipschitz Minty problems.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) GeneralizedMintyExtragradient (Ours) (review) Sufficient budget O(1+(L0R/ε)2+(L1R)2)
(2) EG (Choudhury and Loizou 2025), Thm. 3.6, derived bound under Minty O(1+(L0R/ε)2+(L1R)2) (1): Matches and formalizes the known rate. (2) assumes monotonicity but uses only the Minty inequality at the predictor. (1): Roughly triple the leading budget constant. Freezing needs ε in the updates. Tracking the best iterate in (2) uses existing calls.
(3) EG (Choudhury and Loizou 2025), Thm. 3.8 at ρ=0 O(1+(L0R/ε)2(1+L1ReL1R)2) (1): Polynomial instead of exponential dependence on L1R at ρ=0. Total bound improves for L1R≫1 and Ae1LR≫1. (2) already gives the polynomial bound. (1): Requires Minty. (3) also permits positive weak-Minty relaxation under condition (17).
(4) EG+ (Diakonikolas et al. 2021), Thm. 3.2 at L1=0, ρ=0 O(1+(L0R/ε)2) (1): Matches the rate for L1=0 and covers L1>0, as does (2). (1): No uniform-sample squared-residual guarantee over predictor iterates. (4) also covers weak Minty for 0<ρ<1/(4L0) at L1=0.

Abbr: [x,y] is the line segment from x to y, P is the execution law, and ρ is the cited paper’s weak-Minty relaxation parameter.

Choudhury, Sayantan, and Nicolas Loizou. 2025. “Extragradient Method for (L0,L1)-Lipschitz Root-Finding Problems.” In Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, edited by D. Belgrave, C. Zhang, H. Lin, et al., vol. 38. Curran Associates, Inc. https://doi.org/10.52202/085713-2379.
Diakonikolas, Jelena, Constantinos Daskalakis, and Michael I. Jordan. 2021. “Efficient Methods for Structured Nonconvex-Nonconcave Min-Max Optimization.” Proceedings of the 24th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics, Proceedings of machine learning research, vol. 130: 2746–54. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v130/diakonikolas21a.html.

import LongTails.Setups.MirrorGeneralizedSmooth
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic

namespace LongTails.Setups.GeneralizedLipschitzMinty

open OracleTemplate MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  L0 : ℝ
  L1 : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
  Query p := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
  Reply p := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
  Output p := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.d)
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.L0 ∧ 0 ≤ p.L1 ∧ 0 ≤ p.R ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p F O :=
    (∀ h s x, O.answer h (0, x) s = F x) ∧ Continuous F ∧ MirrorGeneralizedSmooth.SegmentSmooth F p.L0 p.L1 ∧
      ∃ z, F z = 0 ∧ ‖p.x0 - z‖ ≤ p.R ∧ ∀ x, 0 ≤ ⟪F x, x - z⟫
  successful p F X P :=
    Integrable (fun ω => ‖F (X ω)‖) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, ‖F (X ω)‖ ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.GeneralizedLipschitzMinty
